newsitem.title: USA: High winds still disrupting S. Calif. power lines.
newsitem.headline: High winds still disrupting S. Calif. power lines.

text.p: High winds in Southern California continued to disrupt local power lines throughout the day Monday, with around 60,000 homes without power by mid-afternoon, according to local utilities.
The outages were centered in the San Gabriel, San Bernardino and San Fernando Valley regions.
"We are seeing sustained winds of around 20 miles per hour (mph), with some gusts reported as high as 70 to 80 mph," said Steve Conroy, spokesman for Southern California Edison Co.
The winds are forecast to continued throughout Tuesday, he added.
As many as 224,000 of Edison's customers have been affected by circuit interruptions, while around 34,000 remained without power as of 1300 PST, Conroy said.
The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) said 18,000 of its customers had no power as of 1500 PST, compared with up to 60,000 affected since 0530 PST.
"We will continue to work throughout the night to restore power," an LADWP spokeswoman said.
The outages were attributed to falling tree limbs and other debris knocking down distribution lines. No high-voltage lines were affected, the utilities said.
